tagline: Across Missouri on the old Wire Road to the Mississippi.
intro: Route 66 comes in from Kansas and zig-zags through Joplin, partly for traffic and partly because old mines kept caving in under the highway. It winds through Carterville, Webb City and Carthage to Springfield, then goes on by Marshfield, Lebanon and Rolla, past the vineyards between St. James and Sullivan, and on to St. Louis and the river.

East of Springfield it rides an old Osage trail. Settlers strung a telegraph line along it and called it the Wire Road, and when the wire came down, the Old Wire Road. Missouri put up the first historic marker on all of US 66, in Springfield.

moments.title: Devils Elbow
moments.text: Named by tie rafters for a bend in the Big Piney that wrecked their rafts. Its 1923 truss bridge is one of two doglegs left on Route 66, the only one open to cars.

moments.title: Meramec Caverns
moments.text: A cave near Stanton opened to the public in 1935 by Lester Dill, who invented the bumper sticker to promote it.

moments.title: Chain of Rocks Bridge
moments.text: The other dogleg: a 1929 Mississippi crossing bent 22 degrees in the middle to miss a water intake and weak bedrock. Now it carries only walkers and bicycles.
